markdown_report:
Choose the endpoint-preserving cutoff experiment at 30% progress, conditional on establishing a matched control. Its contribution is experimental specification; the supplied historical scores do not establish a control-versus-treatment improvement.

Three starting-point insights guide this choice. First, strict-prefix terminal masking aligns training with appended-MASK inference. Removing the target occurrence and later events prevents bidirectional leakage. Second, cutoff sampling changes observed next-choice exposure. Reserving endpoint probability controls the terminal branch, while reconstruction can add endpoint supervision. Third, current Electronics and Industrial diagnostics show weaker discrimination: wrong-rank rates are 5.71% and 5.37%. Their positive lower-tail margins supersede older negative values; neither establishes validation performance.

Three literature insights organize alternatives. BERT4Rec already includes terminal-mask training [1], limiting novelty. RSS establishes recency sampling [4], but its replacement draws, deduplicated positives and retained later context differ from strict prefixes; inclusion probability is not per-draw probability. TiSASRec and SComGNN motivate temporal and functional distinctions [2,3]. Neither validates this adaptation or establishes ownership, compatibility or current intent.

The framework separates **exposure allocation → temporal representation → candidate suitability**. Cutoffs change exposure; interval biases change representation; jointly learned text features add suitability evidence. Evaluate these separately before combining mechanisms.

Three candidates remain. Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Each cell states a strength and limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Endpoint-preserving cutoffs [1,4] | 2: precise comparison; established ingredients | 6: useful control; limited mechanism identification | 7: current-choice exposure; no compatibility guarantee | 6: targets weaker discrimination; healthy probes limit diagnosis | 5: small sampler; unresolved host integration |
| Bucketed interval attention [2] | 3: BERT adaptation; established principle | 7: temporal flexibility; uncertain timestamp value | 7: stale-interest modeling; mood unobserved | 5: contextual differentiation; geometry is noncausal | 6: compact bias; timestamp interfaces change |
| Joint title encoder [3] | 4: contextual features; familiar components | 7: richer distinctions; sparse supervision | 8: purpose/specification cues; ownership unknown | 5: finer discrimination; false similarities | 7: one network; substantial preprocessing |

Select cutoffs to address broad historical affinity displacing useful next choices and earlier purchases implying continuing demand. These remain hypotheses: assess current-purpose acceptance and duplication rejection with the same twenty users. Quantitatively, target weaker discrimination without diagnosing collapse.

Establish equal, separately target-normalized reconstruction/terminal losses first. Preserve strict-prefix construction in both arms; then change only conditional nonterminal sampling to half uniform and half uniform over the latest ten eligible positions, retaining endpoint probability 0.1. Diagnostic definitions mentioning 0.75 branch allocation describe a different quantity and cannot supply missing training measurements.

Freeze baseline configuration, RNG construction and selection rules before execution. Track target frequency, context length and repetition as potential shortcuts. Preserve one checkpoint/category, fixed seeds, splits, budgets, predictor and diagnostic contracts. Select through unchanged macro validation HR@10; report no unmeasured gains.

idea.description: Test endpoint-preserving recent-cutoff sampling within the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Establish a uniform-cutoff control using identical strict-prefix construction, then change only the conditional nonterminal cutoff distribution. Each experimental trial trains one jointly optimized model per category, and prediction uses exactly one selected checkpoint for each category. Keep interval attention and jointly learned text features as subsequent, separately budgeted alternatives.
idea.motivation: Strict-prefix next-choice supervision addresses two observed user failures: broad historical affinity replacing a supported next choice, and earlier purchases being interpreted as continuing demand. Recent-cutoff exposure might improve current-context discrimination, but cannot establish whether a need is satisfied, equipment is owned, an accessory is compatible, or a musical mood has changed. Current quantitative evidence identifies comparatively weaker sampled discrimination in Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific: wrong-rank rates are 5.71% and 5.37%, with positive tenth-percentile margins of 0.6623 and 1.1272. These current measurements supersede the earlier negative margins quoted in the inspirations. They motivate an experiment without establishing its causal mechanism or a validation gain. User RankMe values near 24 in these categories indicate concentrated variation, not complete collapse or a demonstrated need for rank regularization. At 30% progress, a controlled exposure experiment remains preferable to simultaneously changing objectives, architecture and negatives. RSS is essential prior art, so the contribution should be described as a controlled BERT4Rec adaptation rather than a new recency-learning principle.
idea.implementation_notes:
Baseline integration and reproducibility: The supplied message contains no corrected baseline source. The code below is an executable integration component, not a complete replacement train.py or a claim that training has run. End-to-end reproduction remains conditional on integration with the supplied source. Preserve the host's model, loading, family-specific sample_batch compatibility, optimizer, reconstruction corruption, catalog-loss semantics, checkpoint selection and embedded predictor writer. Before execution, record the actual baseline source revision and resolved batch size, maxlen, architecture, output head, initialization, optimizer, learning rate schedule, weight decay, corruption policy, negative count if applicable, validation schedule and checkpoint-selection rule. Do not infer these from upstream BERT4Rec or diagnostic prose. If the proposed two-branch objective or strict-prefix construction differs from the corrected cold start, establishing it is a separate control-building intervention. Only the subsequent matched control-versus-treatment comparison estimates the cutoff-policy effect. Historical combined scores of 0.5850 do not establish that comparison or a statistically reliable gain.

Prior-art precision: Original BERT4Rec explicitly describes last-item-only training examples and appended-MASK inference. Its official generators differ: gen_data.py provides random-mask training copies and force_last evaluation construction; README-used gen_data_fin.py additionally inserts mask_last training examples per window. Selected-token replacement defaults to MASK in both, despite inherited 80/10/10 comments. The released output head includes a dense activation, LayerNorm, tied embeddings and token-specific bias; its full-vocabulary normalization includes special rows. These observations establish neither the host's architecture nor its denominator. Preserve the host's actual convention. RSS samples multiple positions with replacement, removes selected positions, compacts retained events and constructs a set of positive item IDs; later unselected events can remain context. Its original evaluated adaptations concern GRU4Rec, Caser and SASRec, with BERT4Rec a comparison baseline. It is therefore related exposure-allocation work rather than this exact BERT4Rec procedure.

Sampling mathematics: For RSS, c replacement draws with per-draw probability p_i give position inclusion q_i=1-(1-p_i)^c and expected distinct positions sum_i q_i. Repeated item IDs further merge at item level, yielding inclusion 1-(1-sum_{i:item_i=v} p_i)^c. These are not p_i, c*p_i, or explicit loss weights. The proposed terminal branch selects exactly one event occurrence, so its specified selection probability is also that occurrence's inclusion probability. Preserve repeated occurrences as distinct training positions. Do not import RSS's deduplication, compacted future context, multiple-positive loss, LambdaRank comparison or extra recency weighting; each would define another intervention.

Eligibility and context: Use identical eligible users in both arms: training histories with at least two events. Preserve baseline user sampling conditional on eligibility, document its distribution and count excluded users. Each selected user contributes one reconstruction example and one strict-prefix terminal example to the same jointly optimized network. Reconstruction retains the corrected baseline's corruption procedure, with at least one valid masked target per example through a common documented fallback. If guaranteeing that target changes the baseline, include it in control construction. Terminal inputs exclude the selected occurrence and every later event, retaining up to maxlen-1 preceding events followed by the reserved MASK. Earlier occurrences of the same item remain legitimate context. Require maxlen>=2, preserve left padding and never expose shifted labels elsewhere in bidirectional input.

Objective: Use loss = 0.5 * reconstruction_CE_sum / reconstruction_target_count + 0.5 * terminal_CE_sum / terminal_target_count. These are branch-wide target means, not means of per-sequence means or one pooled target mean. Each user contributes to both branches; 0.5 denotes objective coefficients, not example-sampling probabilities. Empty branches raise an error. If the host instead skips empty branches without redistributing weight, the proposed nonempty-branch construction is part of establishing the control. Preserve the baseline's full or sampled class denominator, special-token treatment, output head, embedding tying, label mapping, collision handling and any sampling correction. Ignoring padded labels does not remove PAD or MASK logits from normalization. Do not add historical-positive exclusions or change output objectives during this comparison. If sampled loss is used, retain its actual procedure and handle positive collisions, including repeated item IDs; do not describe uncorrected candidate CE as corrected sampled softmax or claim correction eliminates all estimator bias.

Cutoff probabilities: For history length n>2, reserve endpoint probability 0.1 at target index n-1. Let m=n-2 denote eligible nonterminal indices 1 through n-2, and k=min(10,m). The control assigns each nonterminal index probability 0.9/m. Treatment assigns 0.45/m plus 0.45/k for the latest k nonterminal positions. For n=2, the endpoint is the only eligible target and receives probability one; count this exception. Policies coincide for n<=12, so record how many eligible users and sampled examples can actually differ. The recent window excludes the endpoint. This is event-position recency, not elapsed-time decay. Reconstruction can also supervise endpoints, so neither total endpoint supervision nor its objective coefficient mass is fixed at 0.1. Do not inverse-probability-weight treatment losses: that would change the intended exposure intervention.

Diagnostic interpretation: Current training_branch_allocation is null in all categories. Approximately 19–20% terminal-position coverage describes only the diagnostic loader and cannot recover runtime allocation. The supplied metric definitions mention both paired sampled-prefix examples and an example-branch probability of 0.75; treat these as protocol descriptions requiring source verification, not measurements establishing the current control. Example allocation, the probability of selecting a history endpoint within a terminal example, and branch loss coefficients are different quantities. Replacing sampled-prefix construction with terminal masks on latest-history windows changes context as well as allocation and cannot establish a probability-only effect. Update diagnostic definitions to accurately describe the implemented experiment while preserving the required interfaces.

Reproducibility and execution: Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Use the same documented data RNG scheme in both arms, separate from model initialization/dropout RNG. The proposed NumPy SeedSequence([42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]) scheme changes original baseline draws and must be disclosed as part of control construction. Category IDs follow the four-category order in the code. Purpose IDs are 0=user selection, 1=cutoff uniforms, 2=reconstruction corruption, 3=negative sampling. Couple user draws and cutoff uniforms across arms, applying each policy's inverse CDF to the same uniform. Where workers are used, seed their libraries and supply a dedicated DataLoader torch.Generator. Match shapes and forward-call order where feasible. Shared uniforms do not guarantee identical realized corruption or hardware-level determinism. Record versions, hardware and determinism settings. Preserve at most 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per executed epoch, the SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior capped at 200, single-GPU execution, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. All controls, failures and diagnostics share the 43,200 GPU-second budget. Keep the same validation schedule and predeclared checkpoint-selection rule. Measure elapsed GPU time and completed steps rather than claiming identical wall-clock cost. Select one checkpoint per category without averaging or score fusion; do not reuse another trial's checkpoints.

Training measurements: Persist actual epoch and cumulative branch example counts, valid target counts, target-weighted CE, objective coefficient masses, endpoint selections and singleton exceptions, eligible/ineligible users, expected and realized cutoff distributions, context-length histograms, target-frequency distributions, repeated-target exposure, policy-distinguishable history fraction and timing. Each nonempty branch contributes coefficient mass 0.5 per step; this is neither loss-value share nor gradient share. Save counters and resolved configuration beside each selected checkpoint and restore them explicitly. Global CE sums divided by global counts differ from the average of per-step branch means. Diagnostic-loader counts do not substitute for these training records.

Diagnostic and predictor contracts: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) using measured metrics and their definitions. Preserve actual view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces. Keep the loader contract (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors B x L, and adapt probes to actual masked-target BERT4Rec inputs. Missing counters remain unavailable rather than reconstructed. This sampling-only intervention requires no inference architecture change: preserve appended-MASK inference, maximum-nonpadding-index readout with LEFT padding, and the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the identical trained model. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Any later head, text or attention change must update training, checkpoints, ModelView and embedded predictor code together.

Validation and qualitative assessment: Select through the unchanged pinned host macro validation HR@10: 200 users/category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Do not inspect hidden tests, alter splits or change the evaluator. No new gains are claimed. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. Record all evaluated configurations, checkpoint choices and evaluation counts; small adaptive wins remain provisional. If host-provided aligned per-user binary hits are available, report paired gained/lost hits and optionally a paired bootstrap with 10,000 replicates, resampling 200 users within each category using identical indices across arms and analysis seed 42. Average category differences equally. The resulting percentile interval conditions on fitted models and fixed candidates, excluding training randomness, alternative negatives and adaptive-selection optimism. Without supplied hits, omit the interval. Sampled HR@10 does not establish full-catalog top-10 usefulness.

Use the same twenty real training users, five per category, for separate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Record willingness to choose now, current-task or mood matches, duplication, quantity, unsupported-project or compatibility rejection, seasonality and format mismatch. Keep ambiguous identity separate from explicit preference rejection. Use only histories, observed timestamps, titles and descriptions. Generic metadata examples do not authorize unavailable reviews, ratings, categories, prices, stores or simulator traits. Do not invent suitability labels or claim improved functional compatibility from transitions alone.

Shortcut learning and limits: Recent cutoffs alter target popularity, repetition, retained context length and possibly optimization speed. Endpoint preservation does not control these mediators, nor does it guarantee recognition of satisfied needs. Inspect training distributions and describe a winning result as the total sampling-policy effect. A later separately budgeted context-matched comparison could investigate context length, acknowledging changed eligibility; timestamp shuffling would apply to a later temporal model rather than this sampler-only trial. Full-catalog user feedback is needed to assess whether sampled-ranking gains address the two stated user failures. Interval attention and a from-scratch title encoder remain plausible alternatives if the matched cutoff experiment fails or has insufficient distinguishable histories; neither is justified solely by concentrated representation spectra.
idea.pseudocode:
import os
import numpy as np
import torch

DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
CATEGORIES = ('Movies_and_TV', 'Industrial_and_Scientific',
              'Electronics', 'CDs_and_Vinyl')
USER, CUTOFF, CORRUPTION, NEGATIVE = range(4)


def data_rng(category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id):
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence(
        [42, category_id, epoch, batch_id, purpose_id]))


def cutoff_probabilities(n, treatment=False):
    # Entry j corresponds to zero-based target event index j+1.
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('History must contain at least two training events')
    if n == 2:
        return np.array([1.0], dtype=np.float64)
    m = n - 2
    probabilities = np.empty(n - 1, dtype=np.float64)
    probabilities[:-1] = 0.9 / m
    probabilities[-1] = 0.1
    if treatment:
        k = min(10, m)
        probabilities[:-1] *= 0.5
        probabilities[m-k:m] += 0.45 / k
    return probabilities


def choose_cutoff(n, u, treatment=False):
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('History must contain at least two training events')
    if not 0.0 <= u < 1.0:
        raise ValueError('Expected uniform draw in [0, 1)')
    if n == 2:
        return 1, 'singleton_endpoint_exception'
    # Reserve exactly the same endpoint region in both arms.
    if u < 0.1:
        return n - 1, 'endpoint'
    m = n - 2
    probabilities = cutoff_probabilities(n, treatment)[:-1] / 0.9
    cdf = probabilities.cumsum()
    cdf[-1] = 1.0
    v = (u - 0.1) / 0.9
    j = min(int(np.searchsorted(cdf, v, side='right')), m - 1)
    return j + 1, 'nonterminal'


def terminal_batch(histories, uniforms, maxlen, mask_id, treatment=False):
    if maxlen < 2 or not len(histories):
        raise ValueError('Require maxlen >= 2 and a nonempty batch')
    if len(histories) != len(uniforms):
        raise ValueError('Require one uniform per history')
    sequences = np.zeros((len(histories), maxlen), dtype=np.int64)
    targets = np.empty(len(histories), dtype=np.int64)
    records = []
    for row, (history, u) in enumerate(zip(histories, uniforms)):
        n = len(history)
        t, status = choose_cutoff(n, float(u), treatment)
        context = list(history[max(0, t - maxlen + 1):t])
        tokens = context + [mask_id]
        sequences[row, -len(tokens):] = tokens
        targets[row] = history[t]
        probabilities = cutoff_probabilities(n, treatment)
        records.append(dict(
            cutoff=t,
            status=status,
            context_length=len(context),
            history_length=n,
            target=int(history[t]),
            policies_can_differ=n > 12,
            expected_selected_probability=float(probabilities[t - 1]),
            target_seen_in_retained_context=bool(history[t] in context),
        ))
    return sequences, targets, records


def final_nonpadding_features(features, sequence):
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions.unsqueeze(0).expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
    if bool(last.lt(0).any()):
        raise ValueError('Empty sequences have no readout')
    rows = torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device)
    return features[rows, last]


def balanced_loss(reconstruction_sum, reconstruction_count,
                  terminal_sum, terminal_count):
    if reconstruction_count <= 0 or terminal_count <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Both branches must contain valid targets')
    return (0.5 * reconstruction_sum / reconstruction_count
            + 0.5 * terminal_sum / terminal_count)


def resolved_epoch_limit():
    epochs = int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))
    if epochs < 1:
        raise ValueError('SASREC_EPOCHS must be positive')
    return min(epochs, 200)

# INTEGRATION CONTRACT: the corrected baseline source is not supplied here.
# This module does not implement its loader, model, CE or predictor writer.
# Preserve preprocessing seed 0 and initialize training with seed 42.
# First establish the uniform control; treatment is a separate trial.
# Each trial trains exactly one model per category. Never combine arms.
# Record the source revision and all resolved baseline hyperparameters.
# Identify eligible users using TRAINING histories only; count exclusions.
# For each category, epoch in range(resolved_epoch_limit()), and
# batch_id in range(200):
#   1. Construct USER/CUTOFF/CORRUPTION/NEGATIVE streams with data_rng.
#   2. Sample users under the baseline distribution conditional on eligibility.
#      Match these draws across arms; each user contributes to BOTH branches.
#   3. Construct baseline reconstruction corruption with at least one valid
#      MASK target per example using the same documented fallback in both arms.
#   4. Draw one cutoff uniform/user and call terminal_batch.
#      Match uniforms across arms, not necessarily realized target indices.
#   5. Encode both branches with the SAME BERT4Rec parameters.
#      Preserve the baseline output head, denominator and negative procedure.
#      Sum reconstruction CE over all valid reconstruction targets.
#      Read terminal features with final_nonpadding_features and sum their CE.
#   6. Apply balanced_loss and perform ONE optimizer update.
#   7. Persist actual branch/target counts, CE sums, coefficient masses,
#      cutoff records, target/context/repetition distributions and GPU timing.
#      Aggregate full expected cutoff distributions by history length/policy;
#      selected-target probabilities alone are not a complete distribution.
# Save one checkpoint/category under the unchanged selection rule, together
# with resolved configuration and epoch/cumulative bookkeeping.
# Restore bookkeeping explicitly for diagnosis; absent counters remain null.
# Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader),
# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), ModelView and sample_batch.
# Loader tensors remain B x L with (None, sequence, positive, negative).
# Keep measured diagnostic-loader coverage separate from training allocation.
# Inference retains up to maxlen-1 history items, appends reserved MASK,
# left-pads and reads maximum nonpadding position using the sole category model.
# Preserve the embedded predictor writer and all four category routes.
# Optional paired bootstrap requires HOST-SUPPLIED aligned per-user hits:
# resample 200 users/category with shared indices across arms, 10,000 times,
# analysis seed 42; average four category differences equally. Otherwise omit.
# Never read hidden tests or other trials, alter evaluation, average checkpoints,
# or add separately fitted scores.

originality.positive: The reserved endpoint probability, occurrence-level strict-prefix construction and matched control define a precise comparison distinct from RSS's replacement sampling and deduplicated multi-positive construction.
originality.negative: Masked reconstruction, terminal-mask examples and recency-biased exposure are established. The proposal is an experimental refinement, with no demonstrated new learning principle.

future_potential.positive: A reliable control can determine whether exposure allocation merits later temporal or suitability modeling and provide reusable measurement of training allocation.
future_potential.negative: The effect combines target frequency, repetition, context length and recency. It may mostly change convergence speed, and sampled HR gains may not improve full-catalog usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The core sampler is small and requires no inference architecture change; preserving the backbone limits implementation scope.
code_difficulty.negative: The previous score of 4 understated unresolved end-to-end integration: baseline objective verification, control construction, matched randomness, persistent bookkeeping and diagnostic consistency remain necessary without supplied source.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item learning, explicitly described last-item-only training examples and appended-MASK next-item inference.
Provides the backbone and supervision principles retained by the experiment.

Official generator behavior differs: https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py adds mask_last training examples, while https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data.py uses force_last for evaluation construction.

Released output-head and vocabulary details are available at https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py and https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/vocab.py; these distinguish paper-level descriptions from executable normalization.
limitations: Does not establish that this endpoint-preserving cutoff policy improves the pinned RecHarness benchmark.
Observed next-item prediction does not verify compatibility, ownership or current-purpose suitability.
Upstream generator and output-head conventions do not establish the corrected host baseline's implementation and must not replace its fixed splits or left-padding contract.

related_work.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models interaction intervals as information beyond sequence position.
Motivates a separate bucketed-gap attention experiment within the retained BERT4Rec family.
limitations: Its original architecture is not the required corrected BERT4Rec.
Unknown next-event timestamps require a history-only convention, such as anchoring the appended MASK to the latest observed interaction, applied consistently during terminal training and inference.
Interval modeling does not imply that older interactions should always receive less attention or establish intent drift as the cause of current errors.

related_work.title: SComGNN: Complementary Item Recommendation
contributions: Distinguishes complementary relationships from broad similarity.
Motivates testing whether jointly learned title and description features can distinguish related items from useful next choices within one network.
limitations: Its graph-based setup does not establish that ordinary sequential transitions identify functional complements.
Reported evidence does not validate a from-scratch text-aware BERT4Rec under these data and evaluation constraints.
Available item text cannot establish equipment ownership, fulfilled needs or unobserved simulator traits.

related_work.title: Effective and Efficient Training for Sequential Recommendation using Recency Sampling
contributions: Provides the closest recency-exposure prior art; official implementation: https://github.com/asash/bert4rec_repro.
Samples target positions with replacement according to normalized recency importance, removes selected positions and constructs a set of positive item IDs.
Makes position inclusion depend on 1-(1-p_i)^c; duplicate draws and repeated item IDs can reduce distinct supervision relative to the number of draws.
Supports multiple-positive losses and compares BCE with LambdaRank, making sampling and loss choices separate experimental factors.
limitations: Unselected events later than an early target remain context, unlike the proposed strict-prefix terminal examples.
Original experiments adapt GRU4Rec, Caser and SASRec; BERT4Rec is a comparison baseline rather than an evaluated RSS adaptation.
Replacement-draw probabilities are not inclusion probabilities or explicit loss weights; removing replacement, retaining multiplicities or adding probability-based loss weights changes the objective.
Does not establish gains for the proposed endpoint-preserving BERT4Rec policy under the pinned four-category benchmark.
